essays.question: Discuss how technology affects relationships between people.

versions.text:
Smartphones, video calls and messaging apps have become part of nearly every friendship and family, and technology has changed how people relate to one another. This essay will explain two key ways in which technology affects relationships: by keeping people in touch across distance and by changing the quality of the time they spend together.

First and foremost, technology helps people to stay in touch and to form new connections. Video calls and messages connect families and friends across distances, and migrants and students abroad can speak to their relatives every day. A grandmother who watches her grandchildren's school play by video call from another country, for example, feels part of their lives. Social networks help people to find others who share their interests or circumstances, such as patients with a rare illness, and online communities can offer support to those who feel isolated in their own neighbourhood. Many friendships that would once have faded can now continue for years.

In addition, technology can weaken the quality of time together. Phones at the dinner table, constant notifications and the habit of checking messages reduce attention, so people may be in the same room without really listening to each other. Online communication can also be shallow, and conflicts can grow when tone is misunderstood in text. Online bullying and the pressure to display a perfect life on social media can harm self-esteem, especially among young people. However, these problems are not inevitable. Families can agree on phone-free meals, and friends can use messaging to arrange meetings in person. Relationships benefit when technology is used to add to face-to-face contact, not to replace it.

To sum up, technology affects relationships in both helpful and harmful ways, and its effect depends on how people choose to use it. For these reasons, it should be used thoughtfully.

essays.question: Some people believe that volunteering benefits society. Others think it primarily benefits volunteers. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Hospitals, schools and charities rely on people who give their time without payment, and opinions differ on whether volunteering mainly benefits society or primarily benefits the volunteers. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters argue that volunteering benefits society. Volunteers provide help that public services cannot always afford, from tutoring to care for older people, and many charities could not survive without them. A retired teacher who helps children to read after school, for example, offers support that the school could not pay for. Volunteering also builds community, since people who work together on a common cause meet neighbours they would not otherwise know and develop trust. In emergencies, from floods to pandemics, volunteers have often made the difference between a coordinated response and chaos. The work also shows that people care about each other beyond family ties.

On the other hand, others point out that volunteers themselves gain a great deal. They learn skills such as organising, communicating and teamwork, which may help them to find paid work, and they gain friendships, confidence and a sense of purpose. For young people, volunteering can provide experience that improves a career application, and for retired people it can reduce loneliness. A retired teacher who helps children to read, for instance, finds new purpose herself. Some critics suggest that this self-interest means volunteering is not truly selfless, although such motives do not reduce the value of the help given.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that volunteering benefits both society and the volunteer, and that this mutual benefit is the reason why it works so well.

essays.question: Some people say that pets are as important as family members. Do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Many owners treat their dogs and cats as part of the household, and some people say that pets are as important as family members. I disagree with this view, since pets give companionship and joy but cannot replace human family members, although their value should not be dismissed.

To begin with, pets give companionship and joy but cannot replace human family members. They reduce loneliness and encourage exercise and responsibility, yet they cannot offer the shared history, conversation and mutual obligations that bind a family. A widow whose dog greets her every day, for example, feels less alone, but the dog cannot replace the conversation of a relative or understand her worries. Family members support one another through illness, financial difficulty and important decisions, and they share memories that stretch over generations. A pet, however loved, does not take part in these exchanges in the same way. Humans also have rights and a moral status that animals, though deserving of kindness, do not share to the same degree.

Furthermore, treating pets as equal to relatives can lead to difficult choices. If a family's time and money are spent on pets at the expense of children or elderly parents, it may cause resentment, and decisions about medical care or inheritance become confusing. Admittedly, pets are important to many people, especially those who live alone, and the grief at losing one can be genuine and deep. Some therapy animals even help to treat anxiety and loneliness. This importance deserves respect, but it differs in kind from the relationships between people. A balanced view recognises pets as valued companions and family members as irreplaceable.

In conclusion, I disagree that pets are as important as family members, because they cannot offer the same relationships or obligations, although they enrich many lives.

essays.question: What are the causes of low birth rates in some countries? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
In many developed countries, the average woman now has fewer than two children, and some governments worry about shrinking populations. This essay will analyse the principal causes of low birth rates and propose realistic solutions.

Low birth rates reflect the high cost of raising children and the difficulty of combining work and family. Housing, childcare and education are expensive, women increasingly pursue careers and marry later, and long working hours and insecure jobs make couples delay or limit families. A couple who postpone parenthood until they can afford a larger flat, for example, may find that they have only one child. In addition, changes in attitudes, such as greater emphasis on personal freedom and careers, and access to contraception, mean that parenthood is a choice made later and less often than in the past. Concern about the future, including climate change and economic uncertainty, also discourages some couples. As a result, many people end up with fewer children than they would like.

To address this issue, governments should make it easier for couples to have the children they want. Affordable childcare, housing support, parental leave for both parents, flexible working and financial help reduce the costs and career penalties of having a child. In addition, employers can be encouraged to offer part-time options and to avoid penalising workers who take leave. Countries that have introduced generous and well-designed family policies, such as in parts of northern Europe, have generally seen higher birth rates than those that have not. Immigration can also help to maintain the workforce, although it is not a complete solution on its own.

In conclusion, low birth rates stem mainly from the costs of raising children and the difficulty of balancing work and family, but practical support for parents offers a realistic way forward.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on early childhood care? Use examples.

versions.text:
The first few years of life shape a child's health, learning and behaviour for decades, and many governments now invest in nurseries and early education. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on early childhood care: better outcomes for children and wider gains for families and the economy.

First and foremost, good care in the early years gives children a lasting advantage. The brain develops fastest before the age of five, and quality nurseries build language, social skills and curiosity. A child who spends mornings in a good nursery, for example, enters school already able to listen, share and speak in sentences. Children from disadvantaged homes benefit most, since they may have fewer books and less conversation at home, so early care narrows the gap before formal schooling starts. As a result, children arrive at school ready to learn, and they are less likely to need extra support or to drop out later. Trained staff can also notice health or developmental problems early.

In addition, early childhood care brings wider benefits to families and the economy. When affordable care is available, parents, especially mothers, can return to work, which raises household income and tax revenue and supports gender equality. Research in several countries has found that every unit of money spent on high-quality early education returns several times as much through better school results, higher earnings and lower costs for health, welfare and crime. Although high-quality care requires investment in staff training and buildings, and poor-quality care can do little good, the long-term returns are large. Countries such as Denmark and Sweden, where early care is widely available and highly regarded, show how a society can benefit.

To sum up, early childhood care brings clear benefits to a country, above all better outcomes for children and wider economic gains. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on childcare or on elder care? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Many countries face two demographic pressures at once: young families need help to raise children, while the number of very old people is growing quickly. This is why opinions are divided as to whether public money should be focused on childcare or on elder care. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of childcare argue that it invests in the future and lets parents work. Good care in the early years builds language, social skills and curiosity, helping children to do well at school and later in life. A child who spends mornings in a good nursery, for example, enters school already able to listen, share and speak in sentences. When affordable care is available, parents, especially mothers, can return to work, which raises household income and tax revenue. The returns on early investment are large, since healthier, better-educated children become productive adults who will support future generations.

On the other hand, supporters of elder care point out that older people have often worked and paid taxes for decades and deserve dignity in their final years. Many suffer from frailty, dementia or loneliness, and without care they may be neglected, while their relatives are forced to cut their working hours. A woman who looks after both her young children and her elderly mother, for example, may be forced to give up her job. With populations ageing, the demand for care is growing fast, and failure to meet it would cause great suffering.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that a balanced budget is wise, with childcare given priority where early investment is most lacking, while elder care is expanded in line with the growth of the ageing population.

essays.question: Discuss the role of parents in children’s academic success.

versions.text:
When a child does well at school, parents often receive some of the credit, and when a child struggles, they sometimes receive the blame. This essay will explain two key ways in which parents influence children's academic success: through encouragement and routine, and through the resources and expectations that they provide.

First and foremost, parents shape children's academic success through encouragement, routine and interest. Children whose parents read with them, set regular times for homework and show curiosity about school tend to achieve more. A parent who sits with a child for twenty minutes of homework every evening, for example, shows that learning matters, and the child sees study as a normal part of life. Praise for effort rather than just results builds confidence and persistence, and a calm home with enough sleep and breakfast supports concentration. Talking to children about books, news and ideas also develops vocabulary and curiosity long before they start school.

In addition, parents provide resources and set expectations. They can buy books, find a quiet place to study, arrange tutors or help with school choices, and they communicate with teachers when problems arise. Realistic expectations motivate children, since young people often try to live up to what their parents believe they can do. However, excessive pressure can have the opposite effect, causing stress, anxiety and a dislike of learning. Parents are also not the only influence, as teachers, friends and the child's own character matter, and children from poorer families may succeed with the help of good schools and committed teachers. Support works better than pressure, and parents should show interest and encouragement rather than demanding top marks.

To sum up, parents play an important role in children's academic success by providing encouragement, structure and resources, provided that they avoid excessive pressure. For these reasons, their involvement should be welcomed.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that children should not use smartphones?

versions.text:
Many children now receive a smartphone before they start secondary school, and some argue that children should not use smartphones at all. I agree to a large extent, since young children are not ready for unrestricted phones, although complete bans are neither realistic nor always desirable for older children.

To begin with, young children are not ready for unrestricted smartphones. Phones distract from schoolwork, disturb sleep, expose children to unsuitable content and online bullying, and replace play and exercise, although they allow parents and children to stay in contact. A ten-year-old who scrolls on a phone in bed until midnight, for example, arrives at school tired and distracted. Studies have linked heavy use among young people to anxiety, low mood and poor sleep, and games and social media are designed to hold attention for as long as possible. Children also lack the judgment to deal with strangers, advertising and pressure to share personal images, and they may not tell adults when something goes wrong.

Furthermore, childhood is a time for activities that phones can replace, such as outdoor play, reading, face-to-face friendship and hobbies. Delaying and limiting use protects health, learning and development. However, a complete ban has drawbacks. Phones can keep children safe by allowing them to call parents, and as they grow older they need to learn how to use technology responsibly, since it is part of modern life. A sensible approach would give young children a basic phone, if any, set clear rules about when and where phones are used, and allow smartphones gradually, with parental controls and conversations about safety, from around the early teens.

In conclusion, children should not use smartphones freely, particularly when young, because of the risks to health and learning, but supervised and limited use as they mature is reasonable.

essays.question: Discuss how volunteering abroad benefits communities and volunteers.

versions.text:
Every year, thousands of people spend weeks or months working without pay in distant countries, from building schools to teaching English, and the benefits of volunteering abroad are often discussed. This essay will explain two key ways in which volunteering abroad benefits communities and volunteers: by meeting real needs and by promoting learning and understanding.

First and foremost, volunteering abroad can help communities if it matches local needs. Volunteers with skills such as teaching or medicine fill real gaps and can bring knowledge, energy and extra hands to projects with limited funds. A volunteer who teaches English in a village for six months, for example, may help children to learn, but unless the project is planned, she may leave before it can continue. When projects are led by local people and organisations, the benefit lasts, because volunteers support community priorities rather than imposing their own. Volunteers can also raise funds and awareness back at home, bringing wider attention to local problems.

In addition, volunteers gain a great deal. They learn about other cultures and ways of life, develop language and practical skills, and often return with greater confidence, maturity and a wish to continue helping. Contact between people from different countries can reduce prejudice and build friendships across borders. However, there are risks. Short, poorly planned visits may take work from local people, create dependence or provide little real help, and volunteers without training can cause harm, for example in orphanages or clinics. Organisations should therefore select volunteers carefully, train them, work with local partners and measure results. Choosing reputable programmes is important for anyone who wants their time to make a difference.

To sum up, volunteering abroad benefits communities and volunteers when it meets local needs and is well organised. For these reasons, it deserves support, but only in responsible forms.

essays.question: Should individuals be responsible for volunteering, or should society/government encourage it? Discuss.

versions.text:
Charities, schools and neighbourhood groups depend on people who give their time freely, and opinions differ on whether individuals should be responsible for volunteering or whether society and government should encourage it. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of personal responsibility argue that volunteering depends on personal motivation. People volunteer when they care about a cause, and a gift of time is valuable precisely because it is freely given. Forcing or pressuring people may produce half-hearted effort and resentment, and a person who is made to volunteer may not value the work. A resident who chooses to help clean a river because she loves the place, for example, is likely to work harder and keep going longer than someone who is told to do so. Voluntary service also reflects a healthy civil society in which citizens, not officials, take the initiative to solve problems.

On the other hand, supporters of public encouragement point out that many people would volunteer if it were made easier. Schools can offer course credit for community service, employers can provide paid time off, and governments can fund volunteer organisations, provide training and recognise the work with awards or tax benefits. Many people do not volunteer simply because they do not know how to start or cannot spare the time. Such support does not remove the voluntary element, but it opens opportunities, especially for young people and those from poorer backgrounds who might not otherwise get involved. Well-run organisations also ensure that volunteers' time is used effectively.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that volunteering should remain a personal choice, but governments, schools and employers should make it easier and more rewarding through practical support.

essays.question: Discuss how family traditions influence identity.

versions.text:
Every family has its own habits, from the way birthdays are celebrated to the stories told at dinner, and these shared customs shape how people see themselves. This essay will explain two key ways in which family traditions influence identity: by giving a sense of belonging and by passing on values and memories.

First and foremost, family traditions give children a sense of belonging and identity. Shared rituals such as festival meals, religious ceremonies and annual trips create a feeling of being part of a group with its own history. A family that cooks the same festival dish together every year, for example, creates memories that tie generations together. Children who take part know that they are connected to people before them and after them, which gives them security and a stable starting point from which to explore the world. Even simple customs, such as a weekly Sunday lunch, can make a child feel that he or she belongs.

In addition, traditions pass on values and cultural heritage. Through stories, songs and customs, grandparents and parents teach respect, generosity, honesty and the history of the family or community, often without formal lessons. Language, food and festivals link people to their culture, which matters particularly for families who have moved to another country. However, traditions can also restrict individual choice if they are applied rigidly, for example when young people feel pressured to follow a career or marriage that their family expects. Healthy traditions are flexible, allowing new generations to adapt them and to add their own. Identity then grows from a balance between inherited roots and personal choice.

To sum up, family traditions strongly influence identity by giving belonging and passing on values, provided that they allow room for individual development. For these reasons, they deserve to be valued and kept alive.

essays.question: Discuss the role of grandparents in child upbringing.

versions.text:
In many families, grandparents collect children from school, cook meals and tell stories, and they are an important part of how children grow up. This essay will explain two key roles that grandparents play in child upbringing: providing care and stability, and passing on values and a link with the past.

First and foremost, grandparents provide care, stability and emotional security. They look after grandchildren while parents work, which saves families money and gives working parents peace of mind. In some countries, grandparents provide a large share of childcare, and in households with a single parent or two jobs, their help can be essential. A grandparent in good health, for example, can help to look after grandchildren and pass on knowledge, which supports working parents. Children also gain from the patience and attention that grandparents often have time to give, and from having another adult who loves them unconditionally and who can be a refuge when there are tensions at home.

In addition, grandparents pass on values, stories and skills. A grandmother who tells stories about her childhood, for example, gives a child a living link with history, and grandparents often teach traditions, language, cooking, crafts and manners. This helps children to understand their roots and to respect older people. However, there are some difficulties. Grandparents may have different ideas about discipline, sweets or screen time, which can cause conflict with parents, and their own health or energy may limit what they can do. Clear communication between generations, and respect for the parents' final say, usually resolve such disagreements. Where possible, children should also be encouraged to contribute to the relationship, for instance by helping grandparents with technology.

To sum up, grandparents play a valuable role in child upbringing by providing care and by passing on values and heritage. For these reasons, their contribution should be recognised and supported.

essays.question: How can governments support elderly people living alone? Suggest practical measures.

versions.text:
In many countries, a growing number of older people live alone, and some of them are isolated, ill or afraid. This essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take, focusing on care and safety in the home and on reducing loneliness and supporting independence.

To begin with, governments should help older people to stay safe and healthy at home. Home-care services, regular health visits, suitable housing and alarm systems reduce risks and allow people to live independently for longer. An eighty-year-old who falls at home and cannot reach the telephone, for example, may lie for hours unless an alarm system calls for help. Nurses who visit regularly can detect illness early, and help with shopping, meals and cleaning keeps people in their own homes instead of moving into expensive residential care. Grants for adapting homes, such as fitting handrails or a walk-in shower, prevent accidents. This costs less than hospital or care-home places and respects older people's wishes.

In addition, authorities should reduce loneliness and encourage social contact. Community centres, lunch clubs, befriending schemes in which volunteers visit or phone isolated people, and cheap public transport help older people to stay connected. Training in basic digital skills allows them to speak to their families by video and to access services online. Equally important, a regular check by neighbours, local officials or postal workers can identify those who are in difficulty. Governments should also ensure adequate pensions, since poverty makes isolation worse. These measures help older people to keep their dignity and reduce the pressure on health services and relatives.

In conclusion, providing safe, supported living at home and encouraging social contact offer the most realistic way of helping elderly people who live alone.

essays.question: Some people believe that online dating benefits modern relationships. Others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Millions of people now look for partners through websites and apps, and some believe that online dating benefits modern relationships. Others disagree. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters argue that online dating widens choice and makes it easier to meet compatible people. People can meet far more potential partners than in their daily circle, filter by interests and values, and begin conversations at their own pace, which helps the shy and busy. A shy engineer who rarely meets new people at work, for example, may find a partner through an app that matches shared interests. Online dating can also help people who live in small communities, who have recently moved or who belong to minority groups with few partners nearby. Many successful couples now meet online, and the stigma that once surrounded the practice has largely disappeared.

On the other hand, critics argue that online dating can encourage deception and shallow judgements. Profiles can be exaggerated or false, people are judged quickly by photos, and an endless supply of choices may reduce commitment, as users keep looking for someone slightly better. Some users face scams, harassment or safety risks when meeting strangers. Constant rejection can also damage self-esteem. Relationships formed through screens may rely too heavily on appearance, and the pressure of presenting an ideal image can make people less honest.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that online dating can benefit modern relationships by widening opportunities, provided that users are honest, take safety precautions such as meeting in public places, and treat others with respect.

essays.question: Discuss how family meals affect children’s development.

versions.text:
In many homes, the evening meal is one of the few occasions when the whole family is together, though it is becoming less common as schedules grow busier. This essay will explain two key ways in which family meals affect children's development: through health and nutrition, and through communication and emotional security.

First and foremost, regular family meals support children's health and eating habits. Children who eat with their parents tend to eat more vegetables and less junk food, and they learn table manners, portion control and the idea that food is something to share. A child who talks about his day at the dinner table, for example, practises telling a story and feels that his parents are interested. Research has linked frequent family meals with lower rates of obesity and eating disorders, and with better school results, although part of this may reflect other advantages of families who manage to eat together. Parents also have a chance to notice if a child is eating too little or too much.

In addition, family meals support communication and emotional security. Conversation builds vocabulary, listening skills and confidence, and children feel that their lives matter to others. Regular time together gives parents opportunities to learn about friends, problems and worries before they become serious, and children who feel connected are less likely to take risks such as substance abuse. However, busy schedules and long working hours make the habit harder, and meals are only valuable if they are relaxed. Arguments, strict control or phones at the table can spoil the benefits. Even a few shared meals a week, with screens switched off, bring real advantages.

To sum up, family meals promote children's development by supporting healthy eating and by strengthening communication and security. For these reasons, families should try to protect this time.

essays.question: Some people prefer to raise children with strict rules while others prefer permissive parenting. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Parents everywhere ask how firmly they should control their children, and opinions are divided as to whether children should be raised with strict rules or with a more permissive approach. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of strict parenting argue that clear rules give children structure, safety and self-discipline. When expectations and consequences are consistent, children know what to expect, learn to control impulses and are protected from risks. A teenager with a clear curfew, for example, knows what is expected and is less likely to stay out in unsafe places. Children who grow up with firm boundaries often do well at school because they learn to concentrate, finish tasks and respect authority. They may also feel more secure, since they know that adults are in charge. Supporters believe that too much freedom early in life can lead to selfishness and difficulty with rules at school or work.

On the other hand, supporters of permissive parenting argue that a relaxed style encourages independence, creativity and close relationships. Children who are given freedom to make choices and are listened to tend to be confident and open with their parents, and they learn from the consequences of their own decisions. Harsh rules, in contrast, can cause fear, secrecy and rebellion, and children may behave well only when watched. Warm and flexible parents build trust, which makes children more likely to seek advice. However, without boundaries children may struggle with self-control and respect for others.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that the best approach combines warmth with clear limits: rules should be explained, applied fairly and relaxed as children mature.

essays.question: Many people say that community festivals strengthen social bonds. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
From street parties to harvest fairs and religious celebrations, communities around the world mark special days together, and many people say that community festivals strengthen social bonds. I agree with this view, since festivals bring neighbours together and create shared memories, although they work best when everyone can take part.

To begin with, community festivals bring neighbours together and create shared memories. People who might not normally meet cook, perform and celebrate side by side, which builds trust, pride in the place and a sense of belonging. A street party where every household brings a dish, for example, lets neighbours who never spoke to each other become friends. Preparation also requires cooperation, since volunteers organise stalls, music and safety, and working together on a common goal strengthens relationships. Shared memories of such events give a community a sense of history and identity that lasts long after the festival is over.

Furthermore, festivals celebrate and preserve local culture, which helps people to appreciate their heritage and to share it with newcomers. They can also bring different generations and groups together, from children to grandparents and from long-term residents to migrants. However, festivals do not automatically strengthen bonds. If prices are high, if the programme reflects only one group or if noise and crowds upset residents, some people may feel excluded or annoyed. Organisers should therefore make events free or cheap, involve people from all parts of the community in planning and consider the needs of neighbours. When these steps are taken, festivals can be one of the simplest and most enjoyable ways to build community spirit.

In conclusion, I agree that community festivals strengthen social bonds, because they bring people together and create shared memories, provided that they are inclusive and well organised.

essays.question: Do the advantages of state-funded childcare outweigh the cost? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
In several countries, the state pays for much of the cost of nurseries and after-school care, while in others parents pay most of the cost themselves. This essay will discuss the advantages and the cost of state-funded childcare before explaining whether the advantages outweigh the cost.

On the positive side, state-funded childcare pays for itself through higher employment and better child development. Parents, especially mothers, can work and pay taxes, children from poorer homes gain early education, and the economy benefits from a more skilled workforce. A mother who returns to work because nursery places are affordable, for example, pays taxes instead of receiving benefits. Good care also helps children to arrive at school ready to learn, which reduces later spending on remedial help, and it promotes gender equality by allowing women to pursue careers. Countries such as Denmark and Sweden, which fund early care generously, have high levels of female employment and strong child wellbeing.

On the negative side, state-funded childcare is expensive, and the cost must be met through taxes, which may fall on people without children. Poorly designed systems may produce low-quality care, long waiting lists or poor pay for staff, and critics argue that some parents would prefer to care for children at home or to receive cash instead. Nevertheless, these concerns can be addressed. Quality standards, trained and fairly paid staff and a choice between types of care make the system effective, and the returns in tax revenue and children's future earnings often exceed the original cost.

In conclusion, the advantages of state-funded childcare outweigh the cost, provided that the system is well designed and maintains high standards.

grade.summary: Bài viết có bố cục rõ ràng, lập luận mạch lạc và đáp ứng tốt yêu cầu của đề bài về mặt nội dung lẫn ngữ pháp. Để đạt điểm cao hơn, học viên cần đào sâu hơn vào việc so sánh chi phí và lợi ích kinh tế.

Một số lập luận về chi phí chưa được khai thác triệt để dưới góc độ tài chính công.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời đúng trọng tâm câu hỏi của đề bài, phân tích cả hai mặt lợi ích và chi phí. Tuy nhiên, lập trường nghiêng về việc lợi ích vượt trội được đưa ra khá gọn trong thân bài thứ ba thay vì phát triển sâu hơn.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với phần mở bài, thân bài phân chia rõ ràng theo lợi ích và chi phí, và phần kết luận. Các từ nối và liên kết giữa các câu, các đoạn được sử dụng tự nhiên và hiệu quả.
feedback.lexicalResource: Sử dụng từ vựng phong phú và phù hợp với chủ đề giáo dục và kinh tế như 'state-funded childcare', 'remedial help', 'tax revenue'. Một số cụm từ chính xác, tuy nhiên có thể nâng cấp thêm một số collocation học thuật hơn.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, kết hợp linh hoạt giữa câu đơn, câu ghép và câu phức. Ngữ pháp chính xác với rất ít lỗi, thể hiện sự kiểm soát tốt các thì và mệnh đề quan hệ.

analysis.type_vi: A/D: lợi thế của chăm sóc trẻ do nhà nước tài trợ có lớn hơn chi phí không (advantages outweigh)

plan.think: Mở bài mô tả thực tế (nhà nước trả phần lớn chi phí nhà trẻ và chăm sóc sau giờ học ở một số nước, cha mẹ tự trả ở nơi khác); phán quyết có điều kiện: hệ thống thiết kế tốt, chuẩn cao.

Tự hoàn vốn qua việc làm cao hơn và phát triển trẻ tốt hơn: cha mẹ (nhất là mẹ) đi làm và đóng thuế; trẻ nhà nghèo được giáo dục sớm; kinh tế hưởng lợi lực lượng lao động có kỹ năng. Ví dụ bà mẹ quay lại làm việc vì giá nhà trẻ phải chăng nộp thuế thay vì nhận trợ cấp. Giảm chi phí hỗ trợ học bù sau này; bình đẳng giới; Đan Mạch, Thuỵ Điển.

Đắt, phải trả bằng thuế có thể rơi vào người không có con; hệ thống thiết kế kém: chất lượng thấp, danh sách chờ, nhân viên lương thấp; có cha mẹ muốn tự chăm hoặc nhận tiền mặt. Nevertheless: chuẩn chất lượng, nhân viên được đào tạo và trả lương công bằng, lựa chọn nhiều loại; lợi nhuận về thuế và thu nhập tương lai của trẻ thường vượt chi phí ban đầu.
Lợi thế lớn hơn chi phí nếu hệ thống thiết kế tốt, giữ chuẩn cao.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that parents should limit screen time for children?

versions.text:
Children today spend hours every day looking at televisions, tablets, phones and games consoles, and many people say that parents should limit screen time. I agree with this view, since too much screen use harms sleep, activity and development, although the aim should be balance, not total prohibition.

To begin with, parents should set sensible limits on screen time because too much screen use reduces sleep, exercise and face-to-face play. A family that keeps phones out of bedrooms at night, for example, finds that children sleep better and arrive at school more alert. Research has linked long hours of screen use with poor sleep, lower concentration, obesity and, in some cases, anxiety and low mood. Young children, whose brains are developing rapidly, need real-world play, conversation and movement far more than passive viewing. Without limits, attractive games and videos designed to hold attention can crowd out homework, reading and friendships.

Furthermore, limits give children a chance to learn self-control and to develop other interests. Children seldom judge for themselves when they have had enough, so parents have to provide the structure until they can do so. However, limits should be reasonable and flexible. Screens can be used for learning, creativity and keeping in touch, and not all screen time is equal; a video call with a grandparent or an educational programme differs from endless scrolling. Rules work best when they are explained, agreed with children and followed by the parents themselves, for example by having screen-free meals. Over time, children can be given more responsibility to manage their own use as they mature.

In conclusion, I agree that parents should limit screen time for children, because excessive use harms health and development, but the limits should be balanced and combined with good example and explanation.

grade.summary: Đây là một bài viết rất xuất sắc với lập luận chặt chẽ, bố cục rõ ràng và ngữ pháp gần như hoàn hảo. Người viết đã thể hiện sự hiểu biết sâu sắc về chủ đề và trình bày quan điểm một cách thuyết phục.

Cách diễn đạt ở một số chỗ có phần dài dòng, chưa tối ưu hóa được độ súc tích.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời rất tốt câu hỏi, có quan điểm rõ ràng ngay từ mở bài và duy trì xuyên suốt. Các luận điểm đưa ra để ủng hộ việc giới hạn thời gian màn hình đều thiết thực và có ví dụ minh họa.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc, các đoạn được phân chia hợp lý với các từ nối tự nhiên. Sự phát triển ý tưởng từ đoạn này sang đoạn khác diễn ra mượt mà và logic.

analysis.type_vi: Agree/Disagree (Extent): cha mẹ nên giới hạn thời gian màn hình của trẻ — agree

plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế (trẻ nhìn màn hình hàng giờ mỗi ngày) rồi agree + lý do + điều kiện (cân bằng thay vì cấm hoàn toàn). Khác đề 146 (điện thoại thông minh) ở chỗ nói về mọi màn hình và vai trò cha mẹ.

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — bảo vệ giấc ngủ, vận động, vui chơi
plan.think: Dùng màn hình quá nhiều giảm ngủ, vận động và chơi trực tiếp; ví dụ gia đình để điện thoại ngoài phòng ngủ ban đêm thì trẻ ngủ ngon, đến lớp tỉnh táo; nghiên cứu liên hệ với ngủ kém, tập trung thấp, béo phì, đôi khi lo âu; trẻ nhỏ cần chơi thật, trò chuyện, vận động; trò chơi, video thiết kế giữ chú ý lấn át bài tập, đọc, bạn bè.

Giới hạn cho trẻ cơ hội học tự chủ và phát triển sở thích khác; trẻ ít tự xét khi đủ nên cha mẹ cho cấu trúc. Giới hạn hợp lý, linh hoạt: màn hình dùng để học, sáng tạo, giữ liên lạc; không phải mọi thời gian như nhau (gọi video với ông bà khác lướt vô tận). Quy tắc hiệu quả khi được giải thích, thoả thuận, cha mẹ cũng theo (bữa ăn không màn hình); dần cho trẻ tự quản khi lớn.
Agree vì dùng quá mức hại sức khoẻ và phát triển, nhưng giới hạn cân bằng, kèm làm gương và giải thích.

essays.question: How can governments improve access to affordable childcare? Suggest practical measures.

versions.text:
For many families, the cost of childcare is as high as a second mortgage, and shortages of places force some parents to stop working. This essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take, focusing on reducing the cost of childcare and on increasing the supply and quality of places.

To begin with, governments should make childcare more affordable. Subsidies paid directly to providers or to parents, tax credits and free hours of early education for all children reduce costs and give families a real choice. A single parent who receives a subsidy for a registered childminder, for example, can take a full-time job instead of relying on benefits. Support should be targeted at those with the lowest incomes, but a basic entitlement for all can avoid stigma and encourage wide participation. Employers can also be encouraged, through tax incentives, to offer workplace nurseries or childcare vouchers.

In addition, authorities should increase supply and ensure quality. Funding for new nurseries in areas where places are short, training and fair pay for staff, and clear quality standards with regular inspections give parents confidence. Low pay leads to high staff turnover, which harms children, so better wages are an investment in quality. Flexible provision, such as evening or weekend care for shift workers, and support for community-based schemes and registered childminders help families whose working hours do not fit standard times. Equally important, flexible working rules for employers allow parents to share care between them. These measures cost money, but they cost less than the benefits and lost tax revenue that result when parents cannot work.

In conclusion, reducing costs and expanding the supply and quality of places offer the most realistic way of improving access to affordable childcare.

Thiếu một số từ nối nâng cao hơn để chuyển ý giữa các giải pháp.

feedback.lexicalResource: Sử dụng từ vựng phong phú, tự nhiên và đúng chủ đề (childcare, subsidies, tax credits, staff turnover, workplace nurseries). Các cụm từ kết hợp (collocations) chuẩn xác và mang tính học thuật.

analysis.type_vi: Solutions only: chính phủ cải thiện tiếp cận chăm sóc trẻ giá phải chăng

plan.think: Mở bài nêu vấn đề (chi phí chăm sóc trẻ ngang một khoản thế chấp thứ hai; thiếu chỗ buộc một số cha mẹ ngừng làm việc); hai nhóm: giảm chi phí; tăng nguồn cung và chất lượng.

Trợ cấp trả trực tiếp cho nhà cung cấp hoặc cha mẹ, tín dụng thuế, giờ giáo dục sớm miễn phí cho mọi trẻ; ví dụ cha mẹ đơn thân nhận trợ cấp cho người trông trẻ đăng ký có thể làm toàn thời gian thay vì sống nhờ trợ cấp. Tài trợ nhà trẻ mới nơi thiếu chỗ, đào tạo và lương công bằng cho nhân viên, chuẩn chất lượng rõ và thanh tra định kỳ; lương thấp gây nghỉ việc nhiều hại trẻ; chăm sóc linh hoạt (buổi tối, cuối tuần) cho người làm ca; hỗ trợ chương trình cộng đồng, người trông trẻ đăng ký; quy định làm việc linh hoạt để cha mẹ chia sẻ; rẻ hơn trợ cấp và thuế mất do cha mẹ không đi làm được.
Tóm hai nhóm.

essays.question: Discuss how family leave policies affect gender equality.

versions.text:
In most countries, women still take more time off than men after a child is born, and this difference affects careers, pay and attitudes. This essay will explain two key ways in which family leave policies affect gender equality: by influencing who cares for children and by changing how employers and society treat men and women.

First and foremost, paid leave for both parents helps to share care and reduces career penalties for women. When only mothers take leave, employers may see women as less committed, whereas fathers who take time off become more involved at home and make childcare normal for both sexes. A father who takes three months of paid leave, for example, learns to care for a baby on his own and shares the load with his partner afterwards. Research in Nordic countries suggests that earmarked leave for fathers, which is lost if not used, increases the share of care that fathers provide, and this leads to more equal division of housework in later years. Women can then return to work sooner and keep their careers moving.

In addition, leave policies shape attitudes and employer behaviour. If both sexes are expected to take leave, employers can no longer assume that only women will be absent, which reduces discrimination in hiring and promotion, and children grow up seeing both parents as carers. However, equality improves only when leave is well paid and fathers are encouraged to use it. Low pay discourages fathers from taking leave, long leave for mothers alone can make women's absence from work longer, and some workplaces still look down on men who ask for time off. Generous, flexible and shared leave, supported by campaigns, is therefore most effective.

To sum up, family leave policies can improve gender equality when they support shared care and change workplace attitudes. For these reasons, they should be designed with fathers as well as mothers in mind.

grade.summary: Bài viết có chất lượng tốt, đạt khoảng band 7.0 với lập luận chặt chẽ, từ vựng đúng chủ đề và cấu trúc ngữ pháp vững chắc. Để đạt điểm cao hơn, người viết cần nâng cấp một số từ vựng mang tính học thuật cao hơn và đa dạng hóa các cấu trúc câu phức tạp.
weaknesses: Một số từ vựng và cụm từ còn mang tính phổ biến, chưa đạt độ tinh tế cao (band 8+).
Cách diễn đạt ở phần thân bài thứ hai hơi dài dòng và có thể được cô đọng lại để sắc bén hơn.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi thảo luận về tác động của chính sách nghỉ phép của gia đình đối với bình đẳng giới. Các ý chính được phát triển logic, có ví dụ cụ thể như các nước Bắc Âu.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với cấu trúc 4 đoạn rõ ràng. Các liên kết từ như 'First and foremost', 'In addition', 'To sum up' được sử dụng hiệu quả để hướng dẫn người đọc.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng ở mức khá tốt, sử dụng nhiều cụm từ chủ đề phù hợp như 'career penalties', 'earmarked leave', 'division of housework', 'employer behaviour'. Tuy nhiên, một số cụm từ chưa thực sự đạt độ tinh tế của band 8.

analysis.type_vi: Opinion/discuss: chính sách nghỉ chăm con ảnh hưởng bình đẳng giới như thế nào

plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế (phụ nữ vẫn nghỉ nhiều hơn nam sau khi sinh, ảnh hưởng nghề nghiệp, lương, thái độ); báo hai cách: ảnh hưởng ai chăm trẻ; thay đổi cách nhà tuyển dụng và xã hội đối xử với nam nữ.

Nghỉ có lương cho cả hai bố mẹ giúp chia sẻ và giảm bất lợi nghề nghiệp của phụ nữ; khi chỉ mẹ nghỉ, nhà tuyển dụng có thể coi phụ nữ kém cam kết; cha nghỉ thì gắn bó tại nhà và khiến chăm con thành bình thường cho cả hai giới. Ví dụ người cha nghỉ ba tháng có lương học tự chăm bé và chia sẻ gánh nặng sau đó. Nghiên cứu Bắc Âu: nghỉ dành riêng cho cha tăng phần chăm của cha, chia đều việc nhà về sau; phụ nữ quay lại làm sớm hơn.

Nếu cả hai giới dự kiến nghỉ, nhà tuyển dụng không thể mặc định chỉ phụ nữ vắng mặt nên giảm phân biệt khi tuyển dụng, thăng tiến; trẻ thấy cả hai bố mẹ là người chăm. Giới hạn: bình đẳng chỉ cải thiện khi nghỉ được trả lương tốt và cha được khuyến khích; lương thấp không khuyến khích cha; nghỉ dài chỉ cho mẹ kéo dài vắng mặt của phụ nữ; một số nơi coi thường đàn ông xin nghỉ; nghỉ hào phóng, linh hoạt, chia sẻ, kèm chiến dịch.
Cải thiện bình đẳng giới khi hỗ trợ chia sẻ chăm sóc và thay đổi thái độ nơi làm việc; nên thiết kế cho cả cha lẫn mẹ.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on family-friendly policies? Use examples.

versions.text:
Governments are increasingly interested in paid leave, flexible working hours, childcare and housing support for families, and these are often called family-friendly policies. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on such policies: better outcomes for children and parents, and gains for the economy and society.

First and foremost, family-friendly policies benefit children and parents. Paid leave, flexible hours and childcare help couples to have the children they want, keep skilled workers in employment and give children a better start. An employee who can start early and leave in time to collect her child from school, for example, stays in her job instead of resigning, and she is less stressed at home. Parents who have time and money to spend with young children can support their development, which improves health and learning. In countries with generous policies, such as Sweden, poverty among children is low and parents report a better balance between work and family life.

In addition, family-friendly policies bring wider economic and social gains. Women's employment rises when childcare is available, which increases tax revenue and household incomes, and employers keep experienced staff instead of paying to recruit and train replacements. Birth rates may be higher where families receive support, which helps to maintain the workforce as populations age. Gender equality also improves, since both parents can share work and care. Although such policies cost money, studies suggest that they pay for themselves over time through higher employment and better child outcomes. Society also benefits, since stronger families produce healthier, more confident citizens.

To sum up, family-friendly policies bring clear benefits to a country, above all better outcomes for children and a stronger economy. For these reasons, they deserve sustained public support.

essays.question: Should individuals be responsible for preventing child labour, or should society/government take action? Discuss.

versions.text:
Millions of children around the world work in farms, mines, factories and homes instead of going to school, and opinions differ on whether individuals should be responsible for preventing child labour or whether society and government should take action. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of individual responsibility argue that ordinary people can contribute. Consumers can choose products that are certified as free from child labour and avoid brands that have been linked to it, which gives companies a commercial reason to check their suppliers. Parents can send their children to school instead of work, and people who see children working illegally can report it. A shopper who refuses to buy goods that are suspiciously cheap, for example, sends a message to manufacturers. Public pressure from consumers and campaigns has in the past persuaded several major companies to change their supply chains. Employers, too, bear responsibility for ensuring that no children work in their businesses.

On the other hand, advocates of government and society action point out that child labour is mainly caused by poverty and can only be ended by action at several levels. Families that need income send children to work, consumers cannot always see how goods are made, and only governments can pass laws, inspect workplaces and provide schools and support for poor families. A ten-year-old who works in a brick factory to help his family, for example, misses school and may never escape poverty. Governments can also make companies publish information about their supply chains and punish those who break the law. International cooperation is needed because goods cross borders.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that governments and companies must take the main responsibility, with consumers and parents playing a supporting role.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: cá nhân hay xã hội / chính phủ chịu trách nhiệm ngăn lao động trẻ em

plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế (hàng triệu trẻ làm việc ở nông trại, mỏ, nhà máy, nhà thay vì đi học) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng chính phủ và công ty chịu trách nhiệm chính, cá nhân hỗ trợ.

Người tiêu dùng chọn sản phẩm được chứng nhận không có lao động trẻ em, tránh thương hiệu bị liên hệ; công ty có lý do thương mại kiểm tra nhà cung cấp; cha mẹ cho con đi học thay vì làm việc; người thấy trẻ làm trái luật có thể báo. Ví dụ người mua từ chối hàng rẻ đáng ngờ gửi thông điệp cho nhà sản xuất. Áp lực công chúng đã thuyết phục một số công ty lớn thay đổi chuỗi cung ứng; nhà tuyển dụng chịu trách nhiệm.

Lao động trẻ em chủ yếu do nghèo, cần hành động ở nhiều cấp: gia đình cần thu nhập cho con đi làm, người tiêu dùng không luôn thấy cách hàng được làm, chỉ chính phủ ban hành luật, thanh tra nơi làm việc, cung cấp trường học và hỗ trợ gia đình nghèo. Ví dụ cậu bé mười tuổi làm ở lò gạch giúp gia đình bỏ học, có thể không thoát nghèo. Buộc công ty công bố chuỗi cung ứng, trừng phạt vi phạm; hợp tác quốc tế vì hàng hoá qua biên giới.
Chính phủ và công ty chịu trách nhiệm chính; người tiêu dùng và cha mẹ hỗ trợ.

essays.question: Should individuals be responsible for ensuring equal opportunities, or should society/government take action? Discuss.

versions.text:
Most people agree that everyone should have a fair chance in life, whatever their background, but opinions differ on whether individuals should be responsible for ensuring equal opportunities or whether society and government should take action. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of individual responsibility argue that fair treatment begins with personal attitudes and choices. Employers decide whom to hire and promote, teachers decide how to treat pupils, and neighbours decide whether to welcome newcomers, so prejudice can be reduced only if individuals choose to judge others on merit. A manager who gives a fair chance to every applicant, for example, widens opportunities for people who might otherwise be overlooked. Individuals can also challenge discriminatory remarks and behaviour in their daily lives, and those who succeed can mentor others. Legal rules cannot succeed unless people accept the principle of fairness.

On the other hand, advocates of government and societal action point out that discrimination is often hidden and structural. Equal opportunity needs fair attitudes from individuals and strong rules and support from government. Only laws, public education and help for disadvantaged groups can change patterns that no single person controls, such as unequal school funding, differences in housing and bias in recruitment systems. A company that removes names and photographs from applications, for example, can reduce bias at the first stage of hiring, and governments can require such practices. Scholarships, free early education and anti-discrimination laws help to give people from poorer or minority backgrounds a real chance.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that governments must take the lead by setting rules and providing support, while individuals make equality real through fair behaviour in daily life.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: cá nhân hay xã hội / chính phủ đảm bảo cơ hội bình đẳng

plan.think: Mở bài nêu đồng thuận (mọi người nên có cơ hội công bằng dù xuất thân) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng chính phủ dẫn dắt, cá nhân biến bình đẳng thành thực tế qua hành vi công bằng.

Đối xử công bằng bắt đầu từ thái độ và lựa chọn cá nhân: nhà tuyển dụng quyết định thuê và thăng chức, giáo viên đối xử với học sinh, hàng xóm đón nhận người mới; định kiến chỉ giảm nếu cá nhân chọn đánh giá theo năng lực. Ví dụ quản lý cho mọi ứng viên cơ hội công bằng mở rộng cơ hội cho người có thể bị bỏ qua. Thách thức lời nói và hành vi phân biệt; người thành công làm người cố vấn; luật cần được chấp nhận nguyên tắc công bằng.

Phân biệt đối xử thường ẩn và mang tính cấu trúc: chỉ luật, giáo dục công, hỗ trợ nhóm thiệt thòi thay đổi mô hình không ai kiểm soát (tài trợ trường không đều, khác biệt nhà ở, thiên vị trong hệ thống tuyển dụng). Ví dụ công ty bỏ tên và ảnh khỏi hồ sơ giảm thiên vị ở vòng đầu; chính phủ có thể yêu cầu; học bổng, giáo dục sớm miễn phí, luật chống phân biệt.
Chính phủ dẫn dắt bằng luật và hỗ trợ; cá nhân biến bình đẳng thành thực tế bằng hành vi công bằng hằng ngày.
